newsitem.title: ITALY: Police led to Gucci killer suspects by informer.
newsitem.headline: Police led to Gucci killer suspects by informer.

text.p: Investigators who arrested the ex-wife of murdered fashion king Maurizio Gucci on suspicion of ordering his shooting said on Monday her own life may have been in danger from the same hitmen.

Gucci's former wife, Patrizia Reggiani Martinelli, her clairvoyant Pina Auriemma and three men were detained on Friday in connection with killing of Gucci, who was shot dead outside his office in central Milan in March 1995.
The three men were named as Ivano Savioni, 40, a hotel concierge, and two men from Sicily, Orazio Cicala, 57, and Benedetto Ceraulo, 34.

A statement read out by Milan's chief of police Marcello Carnimeo at a news conference said that according to testimony from an anonymous witness Reggiani had paid 600 million lire ($375,000) for the contract killing.

The Gucci empire, with its unmistakable red and green motif and intertwined gilt GG logo, grew from a humble saddlery shop in Florence in 1906 into purveyors of luxury leather, luggage, shoes, ties and couture to the rich and famous.

Maurizio, the last grandson of founder Guccio Gucci, was plunged into feuds in the style of the Medicis of mediaeval Florence after inheriting his father's 50 percent share. The company is no longer in family hands.

Police brought in an undercover agent, posing as a killer from Colombia, to help expose the alleged murder plot. All the suspects were also placed under close electronic surveillance in the closing stages of the investigation.
The statement said the suspected killers tried to squeeze more money out of Reggiani after they gambled away their new-found wealth in a casino.

Police swooped after they recorded what investigators allege was a meeting between Savioni and Auriemma at which the two discussed how to extort more money from Reggiani for their part in the Gucci killing and on behalf of the two alleged contract killers, Cicala and Ceraulo.

According to investigators, Savioni and Auriemma discussed enlisting the agent masquerading as a Colombian to intimidate Reggiani and even considered ordering her murder because they feared she might admit her own role to the police.
"The two did not rule out even the physical elimination of the woman, using the expression 'we will have the Colombian bring us her head,'" the statement said.
Reggiani was due to be questioned on Tuesday and Italian newspapers have reported that she is denying involvement.

Public prosecutor Carlo Nocerini told the news conference that police were led to Gucci's suspected killers in January by an anonymous witness who had befriended Savioni and got wind of his involvement with Reggiani in the murder.
Nocerini said Reggiani had been consumed by hatred for her former husband because, among other things, he had not looked after her during a bout of illness.

"She has never disguised the fact that she felt rancour because she felt she had been neglected by her husband while she was ill," said Nocerini, adding that there were also economic motives behind the murder.
"There is everything in an affair like this -- resentment, rancour and money matters," said Nocerini.
